turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same n-i-p (regular) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
# Reasoning from device physics and training trends

**What the training data rewards (top decile, ~17–21%):**
1. **Thin compact SnO2/TiO2 ETLs with fullerene or SnO2-np interlayers** — the best cell (20.85%) is TiO2-c | SnO2-np / Spiro-MeOTAD; SnO2-c | PCBM-60 / Spiro gives 17.3–18.0%. These give deep-enough conduction bands, low trap density, and suppressed hysteresis vs. thick mesoporous stacks.
2. **Interface-passivated Spiro-MeOTAD or PTAA HTLs** — PMMA | Spiro (18.0%), PbS-QD | Spiro (18.6%), graphene-oxide | Spiro (16.2%); PTAA on SnO2-np (18.2%), on BaSnO3 (18.9%). Passivating the perovskite/HTL interface cuts non-radiative recombination.
3. **All-evaporated C60/TaTm doped-transport stacks** — C60;PhIm | C60 with TaTm|F6-TCNNQ gave 17.9%; excellent selectivity and conformal films.
4. **Donor-polymer HTLs on TiO2-c|PCBM** — PCDTBT1 with MoO3|Au reached 19.35%.
5. Au/Ag (or MoO3-buffered) back contacts on glass; carbon contacts, exotic scaffolds, flexible substrates and "none"-HTL devices systematically underperform.

**Matching pool candidates:**
- **c064** (FTO / TiO2-c | SnO2-np / Spiro / Au, spin-coating): near-replica of the 20.85% champion recipe (bilayer TiO2/SnO2 ETL, ideal band cascade, low interfacial recombination).
- **c005** (ITO / TiO2-c | PCBM-60 / PCDTBT8 / MoO3 | Au): direct analog of the 19.35% PCDTBT1 device — fullerene-passivated ETL plus a deep-HOMO polymer HTL with MoO3 buffer.
- **c017** (C60;PhIm | C60 / TaTm | F6-TCNNQ;TaTm / Ag, co-evaporation): the 17.9% doped evaporated stack with Ag instead of Au — same selectivity, marginally worse contact work function.
- **c068** (ITO / SnO2-np | TiO2-np / PTAA / Au | MoO3): SnO2-np + PTAA gave 18.2% in training; the TiO2-np interlayer and MoO3-buffered Au should preserve that level.
- **c043** (TiO2-c | TiO2-mp / DAHI | Spiro-MeOTAD / Au): an ammonium-iodide surface passivation under Spiro — same motif as PMMA|Spiro (18.0%) and GO|Spiro (16.2%), reducing interface trap recombination.

Runners-up (c025, c031, c073, c083) match the 15–16.5% band and were left out.

Final: c064, c005, c017, c068, c043
